title: The Test Pyramid: Your Testing Strategy

scenes.line1: Why do some tests fail more often?
scenes.say: Ever notice some tests break all the time while others never do? What’s behind that difference?

scenes.label: Unit
scenes.sub: Small, fast, isolated tests. No external systems.
scenes.say: Unit tests are quick and focus on tiny pieces of code. They don’t touch databases or outside services.
The test pyramid says you should have lots of unit tests and only a handful of end-to-end tests. Unit tests run fast and rarely break. End-to-end tests are slow and fragile.
Integration tests check if components play nicely. Tools like Testcontainers let you use real databases without messing up production. Keeping tests isolated makes them more reliable.

scenes.question: Why do E2E tests break so often?
scenes.right: They rely on timing, networks, and external systems, which makes them fragile and flaky.
scenes.say: Here’s a classic interview trap: Why do end-to-end tests fail so much? It’s not just because they cover everything—they’re fragile because they depend on timing, networks, and outside systems.
